title: A Right to Collect, Not Automatic Land Ownership
imageAlt: A teaching guide for A Right to Collect, Not Automatic Land Ownership. It distinguishes rights, obligations, actions and evidence limits, not an authentic deed or universal payment schedule.
content:
Encomienda was a colonial arrangement involving rights to collect tribute from specified people or communities, with stated obligations attached. An encomendero was a holder of such a grant. The name of the arrangement should not be read as an automatic deed transferring every piece of community land.

Distinguish the questions: who could demand tribute, who lived in the area, and who held rights in land? They are connected but not identical. Records about collection do not alone settle every land claim. This introduction does not say that land dispossession never occurred; it says that the particular claim needs appropriate evidence.

Try a fictional exhibit label. It calls an encomienda a private estate that automatically made every field and every person the holder's property. Correct the definition and identify what further records would be needed about land or treatment of people.

The diagram describes relationships, not an exact territorial map or a title deed.
clues: The arrangement
An encomienda involved tribute-collection rights over specified people or communities and stated obligations.
The holder
An encomendero held the grant; the title alone does not establish every action that person took.
A separate land question
Collection rights are not automatically ownership of every field. Land claims require their own evidence.
task: Which description avoids confusing encomienda with a land deed?
A tribute-collection arrangement whose land and practice claims need separate evidence
Automatic ownership of every field and every resident
A voluntary gift freely chosen by every household
A modern land registry with identical rules everywhere
reason: Distinguish tribute-collection rights from land ownership. A grant alone does not establish every practice, land claim or household experience.
definition: A colonial grant involving tribute collection from specified people or communities, with stated obligations.

title: Tribute Was Required, Not a Gift
imageAlt: A teaching guide for Tribute Was Required, Not a Gift. It distinguishes rights, obligations, actions and evidence limits, not an authentic deed or universal payment schedule.
content:
Tribute was a payment required under colonial authority. It could be demanded in money or goods according to the rules and circumstances involved. Do not call a demanded payment a voluntary gift simply because an account uses a favorable label.

Forms, rates and arrangements changed across periods and settings. This lesson does not give one universal amount, modern currency conversion or identical rule for every household. Ask the date, place and terms of the record before making a numerical claim.

Use a fictional comparison. One person freely offers a present. Another household is told a payment is required by an authority. Identify what makes these different. The exercise is not a transaction that students must perform and does not award points for extracting resources from people.

A payment record can help investigate collection, but its existence does not reveal every family's ability to pay or show that every person approved of the requirement.
clues: A requirement
Tribute is a required payment under an authority, not automatically a voluntary present.
Forms and context
Money or goods could be involved. Check the particular rules, place and period.
Do not invent a universal rate
One amount in one record cannot supply every household's obligation across the colonial period.
task: Which question best checks a tribute record before generalizing its amount?
What place, period and rules does the payment belong to?
Why must all households always pay the same amount?
Which modern price can be guessed without evidence?
Why does a favorable label make a required payment voluntary?
reason: Tribute was required. Its form and amount need context rather than one invented universal rule.
definition: A payment required by an authority.

title: Stated Duties and Actual Practice
imageAlt: A teaching guide for Stated Duties and Actual Practice. It distinguishes rights, obligations, actions and evidence limits, not an authentic deed or universal payment schedule.
content:
Colonial justifications connected tribute collection with obligations such as protection and religious instruction. A stated duty is evidence of what was expected or claimed, not proof that it was fulfilled. Students can study a religious obligation historically without being asked to practise the religion.

Late-sixteenth-century discussions of tribute debated collection and obligations. These records help show that practice could be disputed even within colonial institutions. The debate is not a complete record of every local voice and does not establish identical conditions in all communities.

Watch how to check a fictional report. A grant lists a duty, while another record describes an unfulfilled promise. Keep the formal expectation and evidence of performance separate. Do not assume the grant proves fair treatment or that a complaint proves the same event happened everywhere.

Ask who wrote the claim, what action is recorded and what further evidence could show the experience of the people affected.
clues: A stated obligation
Protection and religious instruction appeared among stated duties connected with collection.
A practice to investigate
A promise or written obligation does not prove that the promised action occurred.
A disputed relationship
Historical debate about collection and duties is evidence of disagreement, not every community's complete experience.
task: A grant lists protection as a duty. What is still needed to evaluate practice?
Evidence of what was actually done and how people were affected
Nothing, because a listed duty proves fair treatment
A claim that every person approved
An invented speech saying the duty was always fulfilled
reason: Separate stated obligations from evidence of performance. Disputes and complaints require their own context and viewpoints.
definition: A duty someone is expected or required to fulfill.

title: Follow the Effect on a Household
imageAlt: A teaching guide for Follow the Effect on a Household. It distinguishes rights, obligations, actions and evidence limits, not an authentic deed or universal payment schedule.
content:
Collection affects people, not only the totals recorded by officials. To examine an effect, ask what was demanded, what was collected and what resources remained for the people involved. A record of revenue and a record of household circumstances answer different questions.

Try a fictional classroom example. A household has a supply of goods, and a required collection removes part of it. The example supports a change in those goods. It does not supply an authentic historical rate or show the circumstances of every family. No arithmetic amount in this exercise should be treated as a real tax schedule.

The burden would need evidence about resources and circumstances, not only an amount. People could seek relief, negotiate, adapt or resist. Identify a particular action rather than assume a single response from everyone.

Explain the evidence without turning an official's total into every household's feelings or using a fictional family to stand for all communities.
clues: Demand and collection
A demanded amount is not automatically evidence that the same amount was collected.
Household circumstances
An effect on resources needs evidence about the affected people and their setting.
A fictional example has limits
A teaching household is not an original account or a universal historical payment schedule.
task: A fictional household example shows goods removed by a collection. Which conclusion fits?
It illustrates a possible resource effect, not every family's historical burden
It proves one authentic rate for all colonial years
It reveals every resident's private feelings
It means all requested payments were always collected fully
reason: Investigate demands, actual collection and household circumstances separately. A fictional illustration cannot establish universal historical burdens.
definition: A demand or difficulty placed on someone, assessed in their circumstances.

title: Check the Grant, Account and Complaint
imageAlt: A teaching guide for Check the Grant, Account and Complaint. It distinguishes rights, obligations, actions and evidence limits, not an authentic deed or universal payment schedule.
content:
A grant, collection account and complaint are different kinds of evidence. The grant may describe rights and duties. The account may record receipts. The complaint may describe a disputed practice or request a change. Do not make one document answer every question.

An official account and a critic's argument both have purposes and viewpoints. Historical discussions of tribute preserve disagreements, but affected people's experiences may still be incompletely recorded. Compare claims and evidence rather than assuming an official title guarantees fairness or every complaint was resolved.

Try a fictional source check. A complaint says a collection was excessive, while the available record contains no reply. You can report that the complaint was made. You cannot invent the final decision or treat the absence of a reply as proof of every person's consent.

Keep place and time attached to the claim. This lesson introduces evidence questions; it does not settle every land dispute, collection rate or history of resistance.
clues: Different records
A grant, receipt and complaint support different questions about the arrangement and its practice.
An unresolved outcome
A complaint or request does not establish that relief was granted or that everyone agreed.
Missing voices
Compare purposes and viewpoints and state whose experience remains uncertain.
task: A complaint about collection has no surviving reply in the exercise. What should the report say?
The complaint is recorded; its resolution needs further evidence
The complaint definitely succeeded
Every affected resident agreed with every demand
A missing reply proves that no complaint existed
reason: Identify what each record supports. A complaint, grant or receipt alone cannot establish the whole outcome or everyone's experience.
definition: A statement raising a problem or asking for a remedy.

title: Build Your Tribute Evidence Report
imageAlt: A report guide separates a tribute arrangement, stated obligations, actual collection and effects on people. The chapter challenge remains unfinished.
content: Connect the arrangement with its practice. Define encomienda without converting it into automatic ownership of every field. Identify tribute as required payment, then ask which place, period and rules a record concerns. Separate collection rights and stated duties from what people actually did. Next investigate effects. What was demanded? What was collected? Whose resources and experiences are recorded? A grant, account and complaint may each help, but none automatically represents everyone. Do not invent a universal amount or an unrecorded outcome. Use this fictional report frame: The record describes [right, duty or action]. Evidence about [place and period] supports [specific claim]. To assess effects on [people], we still need [missing evidence]. This is a classroom tool, not an original quotation. The five-question quiz checks these ideas. Revisit difficult topics and use targeted practice before retrying. Passing earns the mission reward once. Complete all missions, then pass the chapter challenge to earn the chapter badge.
clues: Define the arrangement
Distinguish collection rights from automatic land ownership and required payments from gifts.
Investigate practice
Compare stated duties, demands, actual collection and effects on people.
State the limit
Keep historical context and source viewpoints visible instead of inventing a universal rate or outcome.
task: Which explanation best fits the investigation?
Separate collection rights, required payments, duties, actual practice and household evidence
Treat an encomienda as automatic ownership of all land and people
Call every required payment a voluntary gift
Assume one complaint proves every final outcome
reason: A supported report distinguishes the arrangement, its rules, actual actions and evidence of effects without erasing uncertainty.
definition: A record of payments or goods received, whose context and completeness must be checked.
